title: fix(i18n): retire the orphaned report.editor.* namespace, 105 keys across ten packs (#4145)
body:
Fixes #4145

Retires `report.editor.*` down to the one key that has a reader. 105 keys removed from each of the ten locale packs — **1050 removals**, ~1050 translated strings — with `report.editor.panelTitle` untouched in all ten.

## Premise re-verification — the deletion license

Re-measured on this tip (`6eb40b8d7`), per key rather than by spot check. Of the namespace's **106** leaf keys (confirmed 106 in all ten packs, not 106 plus `panelTitle`), exactly **five** appear anywhere outside the packs, CHANGELOGs and `.changeset/`:

| Key | Where | Is it a consumer? |
|---|---|---|
| `panelTitle` | `ReportConfigPanel.tsx:150,154` + its pin test | **yes — the expected survivor** |
| `title` | one test line, otherwise prose comments | no `t()` call — contrast value |
| `titlePlaceholder` | prose comment only | no |
| `fieldPickerAdd` | `residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx:516` | no `t()` call — translation-provenance anchor |
| `objectName` | `residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx:566-567` | no `t()` call — concept-neighbour premise |

**No `t()` call site reads any of the 105.** No dynamic `t(...)` template form exists in the namespace (repo-wide search for the `report.editor.${...}` construction: zero). No JSON or MDX reference. The premise holds and the license stands.

### One honest correction to the filing's method

The filing's grep was `grep -rn "report\.editor\." packages/ apps/ examples/ scripts/ | grep -v packages/i18n` — it excluded `packages/i18n` wholesale, because that is where the keys live. That exclusion also hid the two **provenance anchors** in `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx`, which the filing therefore never reported. They are not consumers in the rendering sense — nothing renders them — but they are real references that had to be dispositioned, so they are named here rather than left to CI.

This is the same collateral class PR #4168 handled when the slice-3546 test referenced its retired namespace; it is expected shape, not an unexpected consumer, so it did not trip the "stop and report" condition.

## The three test-side references, dispositioned individually

Not batch-rewritten — each was judged on what it was actually pinning.

1. **`ReportConfigPanel.panelTitle.test.tsx`** (#4118's regression pin) read `en.report.editor.title` as the value the panel must **not** be labelled with. What it guards is a rendered **string**, not a key, so `TITLE_FIELD_LABEL` becomes the literal `'Title'` and the pin keeps its full force. The premise guard drops its now-tautological half (`TITLE_FIELD_LABEL === 'Title'`) and keeps `PANEL_NAME !== 'Title'`, which is the half that can still move. A new case asserts the wrong slot is **absent** rather than merely unused — retiring the key removed the original defect's mechanism.

2. **`residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx` REUSED row** `['detail.add', 'report.editor.fieldPickerAdd']` — **dropped**, not re-anchored. Measured: after the deletion `detail.add` is the **only** key in `en` whose value is `"Add"`, so the "one English string, two renderings" failure that list guards has no second site left to occur at. Re-anchoring to a key with a different English string would have invented a premise instead of pinning one.

3. **`residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx` concept neighbour** `report.editor.objectName` — **re-anchored** to `appDesigner.dataSource`, which carries the premise unchanged: it is byte-identical to the retired key in all nine non-`en` packs (differing in `en` only as `"Data Source"` vs `"Data source"`). The premise rests on a ru singular-vs-plural contrast, and `appDesigner.dataSource` ru is the same `Источник данных` against the nav's `Источники данных`. Zero coverage lost.

## The survivor

`report.editor` stays a live namespace holding exactly `panelTitle` — deliberately **unlike** #3811's retirement, where the whole root went. `en` gains a comment saying the single key is by design and that the namespace must not grow back.

## Gates as harness

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:i18n-drift` | exit 0 — **"0 en value(s) changed (0 key(s) added, 105 removed)"** |
| `check:i18n-keys` (all five classes) | exit 0 — 3484 call sites, 2306/2306 literal keys resolve, 62 dynamic-key sites (none in this family) |
| `all-locales-key-parity` | green (inside the i18n run) |
| `vitest run packages/i18n/` | 36 files, **638 passed** |
| `vitest run packages/app-shell/ packages/plugin-report/` | 328 files, **3100 passed**, 1 skipped, 0 failed |
| `type-check` downstream sweep, **prefix** `'...@object-ui/i18n'` = consumers | **35 projects in scope, 0 TS errors** |
| `lint` — i18n + app-shell | **0 errors** (2268 pre-existing warnings, none in changed files) |
| `check-changeset-presence` / `-fixed` / `-no-major`, `check-control-bytes` | all exit 0 |

The drift gate's `105` counts the **`en` key set**; the tree change is 1050 pack/key pairs (105 x 10). Both numbers are stated so neither reads as the other.

`plugin-report` is included because it is the nearest consumer surface — confirmed nothing there reads a retired key.

## `TranslationKeys` narrows — sweep direction and non-vacuity

`TranslationKeys = typeof en`, exported from `@object-ui/i18n` and re-exported by `@object-ui/react`, so removing keys **narrows an exported type**. The sweep above is the **prefix** direction on purpose (`'...@object-ui/i18n'` = the 35 packages that depend on i18n; the suffix form would have swept upstream dependencies, the opposite direction).

The full workspace was built before any of it was judged. Worth recording: the first attempt built only `'...@object-ui/i18n'` and `@object-ui/collaboration` failed with `Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'` — a **filter-closure artifact**, not a regression, because `types` is not a *dependent* of i18n and so was excluded while a genuine downstream consumer needed it. Building the full workspace resolved it.

Reverse-verified against a stale-`.d.ts` false green with a temporary probe reading `TranslationKeys` **through a downstream consumer**. One error, and it carries both directions at once:

```
src/__probe__/tk-probe.ts(12,49): error TS2339: Property 'title' does not exist
  on type '{ readonly panelTitle: "Edit report"; }'.
```

The retired key errors, while the printed type shows the emitted `.d.ts` is fresh and `panelTitle` still resolves to its literal (`const kept: Kept = 'Edit report'` type-checked silently). A stale or empty `.d.ts` would have failed the kept half too. Probe deleted before commit.

## Negative pin, and the reverse verification

`packages/i18n/src/__tests__/report-editor-retired-4145.test.ts` names all **105** retired keys rather than counting them (a count passes when one key returns and another leaves), asserts the root still holds exactly `['panelTitle']`, checks the survivor is a real translation across writing systems, and scans app-shell / plugin-report / components for any `t()` reading a retired key.

This has to be a negative pin because every existing i18n gate runs **call site to key** and none can see a key with no call site: `check:i18n-keys` never visits an unreferenced key, `all-locales-key-parity` is perfectly happy with 105 dead keys present in all ten packs, and `check:i18n-drift` only fires when an `en` value changes. That is exactly how the namespace stayed green while dormant.

**The red set was predicted before the probe ran, and matched exactly.** Reviving `report.editor.title` in `zh` alone:

```
× zh defines no key that en lacks
    AssertionError: zh has 1 key(s) absent from en:
    expected [ 'report.editor.title' ] to deeply equal []
× no pack defines any retired key, in any of the ten packs
    AssertionError: expected [ 'zh :: report.editor.title' ] to deeply equal []
× the namespace root survives holding exactly the one live key
    AssertionError: zh: expected [ 'panelTitle', 'title' ] to deeply equal [ 'panelTitle' ]

Test Files  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
      Tests  3 failed | 29 passed (32)
```

Two independent gates, three assertions — and `ReportConfigPanel.panelTitle.test.tsx` correctly **stayed green**, because it reads `en` and the revival was in `zh`. That asymmetry was predicted too; it is what shows the pin discriminates by pack rather than firing on any change. Restored, and the i18n suite is 638 green again.

### One deliberate design note on the reader scan

Comments are **not** stripped before the scan. A comment stripper that mishandles a `//` inside a string literal drops real code from the scan, and a false negative is the one direction a revival gate must not fail in. The cost is a prose constraint, and it is a live one: the panelTitle test's header originally quoted the defect as a spelled-out call and tripped this assertion during development. Documentation now names a key rather than spelling a call around it, and the failure message says so, so the next author gets a diagnosis instead of a puzzle.

## Changeset

`@object-ui/i18n` **minor** — published keys removed, narrowing an exported type. Same shape the #4168 precedent argued. No user-visible string changes: these keys never rendered.

Per objectui#3724 no `skip-changeset` label is applied (decorative in this repo).
